parties:
Bangladesh ------ Appellant 
vs.
Haji Mozaffaruddin ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
3. The relevant facts of the case are that the plaintiff took lease of the two suit fisheries for 3 years pile for 1376-78 B.S. at an annual rental of taka 6000/- and 4,225/- respectively. The plaintiffs case is that he entered into possession of the fisheries and took all steps for rearing fishes by spending huge amount of money but he could not catch the fishes, due to the civil disturbance in the country in 1971 and 1972, as the Pak Army prevented him from fishing and took away the fishes before the liberation and the local villagers after the liberation of Bangladesh, due to the lawlessness prevailing in the country at that time. The plaintiff brought this fact to the notice of the Sub-divisional Magistrate, Habiganj and other authorities, seeking redress, but they failed to give protection and as a result, die plaintiff could not catch any fish whatsoever from the suit fisheries for the period of lease although, he paid rent in full and in addition incurred huge expenses for rearing the fishes. In view of the above, the plaintiff filed petition for extension of the period of his lease for another pile of 3 years from 1379-1381 B.S. without any rent and the Board of Revenue was pleased to stay auction sale of the suit fisheries and called for a report from the A.D.C. (Rev) Sylhet. The local officials recommended the extension of lease in favour of the plaintiff but the Government suddenly issued instruction for settlement of the fisheries with co-operative societies by auction before 31st May and in view of the above instruction of the Government, defendant No.2 the Board of Revenue vacated the stay order. The above instruction of the Government and the order of the Board of Revenue is illegal, without jurisdiction and against the principles of equity, justice and fairplay and the specific provision of the Estate Manual. The plaintiff therefore, filed the suit for the reliefs mentioned above. 

 4. Defendant No.1, the People's Republic of Bangladesh contested the suit by filing a written statement, inter alia on the grounds that the suit is not maintainable in its present form, that it is barred by the principles of estoppel, waiver, and acquiescence and under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and the plaintiff has got no cause of action. The defendant denied the allegations and statements made in para 1 to 6 to the plaint. The defence case in short is that the plaintiff enjoyed the fisheries for the entire period from 1376-78 B.S. and there is no rule or law for extension of any lease beyond the period of the lease, for any loss sustained by the lessee. The defendant is not responsible for the loss, if any sustained by the plaintiff. The plaintiff might file suit for compensation but the present suit for extension of lease, is not maintainable. The plaintiff did not suffer any loss and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 Mr. Moazzem Hossain, the learned Deputy Attorney General has taken me through the pleadings, the judgments of the courts below and other relevant papers. He contends that even assuming the statements of the plaintiff made in the plaint that he could not catch fishes for the lease period due to the obstruction created by the Pak. Army and the local people before arid after the War of Liberation of Bangladesh, as correct he cannot claim any extension of lease and or injunction as prayed and granted by the courts below, as the appellant Government is not responsible for the loss or injuries, if any, sustained by the plaintiff-respondent, as the loss occurred due to war or vis major or Act of God. He also contends that under section 76 of the State Acquisition &Tenancy Act, the Government has got the exclusive right to settle the suit fisheries in the manner, they like and the court cannot grant any lease or extend the lease in the manner done by the impugned judgments. The relevant portion of section 76 of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act runs as follows: 

 8. Rules 202-206 of the Government Estate Manual, 1958 laid down the procedure for leasing	out fisheries. By Memo. No. FM. 373/73/1219(38)-JM. dated Dhaka, the 1st August 1973, the above rules have been superseded and revised principle of lease of Government fisheries, rules and instructions thereunder have been laid down. In rule I, it is stated that all Government fisheries shall be leased out by negotiation with registered Co-operative Societies formed by genuine fisher-men and preference should be given to the primary societies amongst Fisher Mens Cooperative Societies. It is admitted and it also seems from the above memo that the suit fisheries were not leased out to the respondent, inspite of the recommendation of the officers in the lower level for a further period of 3 years from 1379-81 B.S. In view of the above policy of the Government laid down in the memo quoted above, there is no rule or a regulation not to speak of law to the effect that the respondent-plaintiff was entitled to get lease of the suit fisheries for a further period of 3 years from 1379-81 B.S. for the reasons alleged by him. The learned Munsif observed as follows :- 

 "Article 205 of the Govt. Estates Manual provides for a negotiated settlement. Of course, the circumstances under which the said provision provides for negotiated settlement docs not cover the ptffs' case but from the analogy of the provision it can be said that the ptff suffered substantial loss for no fault of his although he paid rents to the Govt.for the lease period and in the circumstances of the case I think on equitable ground the ptffs' case should have been considered by the Govt. But strange, the then authority of the Govt. i.e. Board of Revenue did not even reply to the pltfs application in spite of the recommendations by the A.D.C. (Rev), Sylhet rather it passed a general order for putting the fisheries in auction. 1, therefore, find the Govt. did not consider the specific case of the plff. although the case had a good merit on the face of it as recommended by the Govts. own officers." Relevant portion of Rule 205 of the Estate Manual, 1958 runs as follows :-- 

 9. it seems that the learned Munsif referred to the later portion of Rule 205(3) of the Estate Maunal quoted above. 

 10. In the present case, it is admitted that the respondent got the lease on auction as per the provision of rule 205(1) of the Estate Manual as quoted above. It is further admitted that the plaintiff was put in possession of the suit fisheries by the Government and there was no dispute about the title of the Government in the suit fisheries or any injunction from any court prohibiting the respondent rom post-that’s easing the suit fisheries. So, the principles laid down in rule 205 of the Estate Manual as referred to by the learned Munsif, is not applicable in the facts of the present case, which fact is also admitted by the learned Munsif. As already stated, the recommendation for giving further lease of the suit fisheries to the respondent for 3 years from 1378-81 B.S. was rejected due, to the change of laws and rules regarding the settlement of fisheries by Memo. No. 1M 3073/73/1219/(38) JM dated Dhaka 1st August, 1973. Thus, it is clear that no rule or law was violated by the Government in refusing the lease to the respondent in the manner alleged, as the Appellant Government is not bound by any law or rule in this respect to give further settlement of the suit fisheries to the respondent for the period from 1378-81 B.S. as claimed. The courts below also did not or could not cite any breach of contract, law, rule or privilege by the Appellant-Government in refusing the lease to the respondent The courts below passed the decree against the appellant as an equitable relief as he allegedly suffered loss for the period from 1376-78 B.S. for reasons stated above. Under section 76 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as quoted earlier, the Appellant Government has got the sole right to lease the suit fisheries in any manner it likes and the court has got no jurisdiction to entertain any application or suit covering any matter relating to the settlement.
